_note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21 (Security deposits), retrieved verbatim from cga.ct.gov on 2026-06-05. § 47a-21(b): max two months' rent (under 62), one month (62+); (a)(11) defines 'security deposit' as any advance rental payment except first month's rent or a key/special-equipment deposit; (c) the deposit remains the tenant's property; (d) returned with accrued interest minus the value of damages from the tenant's failure to meet 'tenant's obligations' ((a)(14)), within 21 days of termination or 15 days after a written forwarding address, whichever is later. status=draft-unverified.

rules.title: Security deposit exceeds the legal maximum
rules.description: Per § 47a-21(b), a security deposit may not exceed two months' rent (one month's rent if the tenant is 62 or older). A clause demanding more is unenforceable as to the excess.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord can't make you pay more than two months' rent as a security deposit — just one month if you're 62 or older. If the lease asks for more, that extra isn't enforceable.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(b)
citations.quote: (b) Amount of security deposit. (1) In the case of a tenant under sixty-two years of age, a landlord shall not demand a security deposit in an amount that exceeds two months' rent. (2) In the case of a tenant sixty-two years of age or older, a landlord shall not demand a security deposit in an amount that exceeds one month's rent.

rules.title: Non-refundable security deposit
rules.description: Under § 47a-21(c) the deposit remains the tenant's property, and under § 47a-21(d) it must be returned with accrued interest, minus only the value of damages from the tenant's failure to meet their obligations. Labeling a security deposit 'non-refundable' contradicts the statutory return scheme and is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: A security deposit isn't a fee — it's your money being held. Calling it 'non-refundable' doesn't make it so; you're owed it back, with interest, minus any real damage or unpaid rent.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(c) & (d)
citations.quote: Any security deposit paid by a tenant shall remain the property of such tenant … (d) … the person who is the landlord at the time a tenancy is terminated … shall pay to the tenant … (A) The amount of any security deposit … less the value of any damages … as a result of such tenant's failure to comply with such tenant's obligations; and (B) any accrued interest.

rules.title: Non-refundable cleaning / redecorating / amenity fee (disguised deposit)
rules.description: A charge that functions as a disguised security deposit may be subject to the § 47a-21(b) cap and return rules; § 47a-21(a)(11) defines a security deposit broadly as 'any advance rental payment' other than first month's rent or a key/equipment deposit. A flat non-refundable cleaning/redecorating/amenity fee is a gray area worth checking. (Move-in/move-out and application fees are separately barred — see ct-fees-001/002.)
rules.tenant_explainer: Watch for non-refundable 'cleaning' or 'amenity' fees — depending on how they work, they may really be a security deposit in disguise, which has to follow the deposit rules (cap, interest, return).

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(a)(11) & (b)
citations.quote: 'Security deposit' means any advance rental payment, or any installment payment collected pursuant to section 47a-22a, except an advance payment for the first month's rent or a deposit for a key or any special equipment.

rules.title: Security deposit automatically forfeited if the tenant breaks the lease
rules.description: Under § 47a-21(c) the deposit remains the tenant's property and under § 47a-21(d) is returnable minus only the value of actual damages; under § 47a-11a a landlord must mitigate by re-renting. A clause making the deposit automatically forfeited on early termination — divorced from actual damages — is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: Breaking your lease doesn't mean your landlord just keeps your whole deposit. It's still your money; they can only keep what covers actual damage or rent they couldn't recover after trying to re-rent.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(c) & (d)
citations.quote: Any security deposit paid by a tenant shall remain the property of such tenant … (d) … shall pay to the tenant … the amount of any security deposit … less the value of any damages … as a result of such tenant's failure to comply with such tenant's obligations; and … any accrued interest.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-11a — duty to mitigate
citations.quote: If the tenant abandons the dwelling unit, the landlord shall make reasonable efforts to rent it at a fair rental in mitigation of damages.
